追.meaning: A <part>snowman</part> on a tea tray shoots down a long icy <part>ramp</part> after his own carrot nose, which bounced off when he sneezed. Faster and faster he slides, stick arms flailing, gaining on it inch by inch. Nothing will stop him in this <kanji>chase</kanji>.
追.on: At the bottom he finally pinches the runaway carrot with a pair of <sound>twee</sound>zers and pops it back on his face.
追.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps the snowman as the carrot slips from his grip again and skids off downhill, and away he goes after it.

抜.meaning: Your <part>friend</part> is wedged tight in a narrow cave, so you hook a ship's <part>anchor</part> to her boots and let a passing tugboat tow it. The rope twangs, the rock groans, and with a loud pop she shoots free. She's managed to <kanji>slip out</kanji>.
抜.on: As she pops free, a <sound>butt</sound>on flies off her coat and pings off the tugboat's horn.
抜.kun: Still dizzy, she crawls into a cosy <sound>noo</sound>k on the deck to catch her breath.

害.meaning: A storm tears the <part>TV antenna</part> off the <part>roof</part>, and it drops straight into the wide <part>mouth</part> of a man yawning on the porch below. One chipped tooth, one bent antenna, no signal for the match. The storm did a lot of <kanji>harm</kanji>.
害.on: His <sound>gui</sound>de dog drags the bent antenna far out into the garden, growling at it as if it were a burglar.

職.meaning: Your new job: stand beside the <part>war gong</part> all day with one <part>ear</part> pressed against it, listening for the faint hum that means trouble is coming over the hills. It's dull, but it pays, and nobody else wants it. It's your <kanji>post</kanji>.
職.on: One day you lean in too close just as someone strikes it, and the boom hits you like an electric <sound>shock</sound>.

未.meaning: A young <part>tree</part> has sprouted one short new branch above its old one, still too thin to hold a bird. A sparrow lands, the twig bends, and the sparrow hops off in a huff. Come back next spring: it's <kanji>not yet</kanji> ready.
未.on: Below, a <sound>mee</sound>rkat stands on tiptoe, waiting for the branch to grow strong enough to be its lookout.
未.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, can I perch on it now?' asks the little sparrow. Its mother shakes her head and says it again: not yet.

球.meaning: The <part>king</part> is bored at his birthday feast and makes one <part>request</part>: something round that bounces. The servants search the castle and come back with the golden orb from his crown, which he dribbles down the hall. Finally, a <kanji>ball</kanji>.
球.on: Then he grabs a pool <sound>cue</sound> and sends the golden ball cracking across the throne room into a suit of armour.
球.kun: It rolls under a <sound>ta</sound>co cart in the courtyard, and the king calls for his <sound>ma</sound>ma to fish it out.

必.meaning: Every morning at seven, a <part>slash</part> of lightning strikes the same <part>heart</part> painted on the old barn door. Rain or shine, summer or winter, it never misses once. The farmers set their clocks by it: it happens <kanji>invariably</kanji>.
必.on: A <sound>hitch</sound>hiker waits by the barn each morning, knowing the flash will light up the road for the first car.
必.kun: Right after the flash, without fail, the farmer fries a <sound>ca</sound>rp, warms some <sound>na</sound>an and cheers '<sound>Rah</sound>, breakfast!'

冊.meaning: Someone has fitted a football <part>goal</part> into a tall wooden <part>frame</part> and filled it with giant leather books instead of a net. Every shot you score knocks one out onto the grass with a thud. Each is a dusty, heavy <kanji>tome</kanji>.
冊.on: Inside the cover of one, someone has pressed a flat, dried <sound>sats</sound>uma as a bookmark.
冊.kun: The goalkeeper reads it curled up on a <sound>fu</sound>ton, with a <sound>mee</sound>rkat peeking over her shoulder.

論.meaning: In the hushed <part>library</part>, two scholars burst into loud <part>speech</part>, waving scrolls and jabbing fingers at each other's noses. Books tumble off the shelves and the librarian shushes in vain. Neither will back down in their <kanji>argument</kanji>.
論.on: One scholar gets so cross he hurls a b<sound>ron</sound>ze bust of an old thinker across the room.
論.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, <sound>ge</sound>t out!' snaps the librarian, then sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' in the dust, while they keep yelling '<sound>Rah</sound>!': picking holes in each other.

容.meaning: A whole <part>valley</part> of soft wet clay sits under a glass <part>roof</part>, and a giant sculptor presses the roof down like a cookie cutter. When she lifts it, the clay has a neat new shape: hills, river and all. She gave the valley its <kanji>form</kanji>.
容.on: From the clay riverbed she pulls a tiny <sound>yo</sound>-yo and lets it sink slowly down its string and climb back up.
容.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' squeals a mouse as she puts the yo-yo into its little hiding box: put in for safe keeping.

振.meaning: A diver hooks a giant <part>clam</part> on the end of an <part>anchor</part> and shakes it hard over the deck. Rattle, rattle: out tumbles a pearl, then a crab, then a rusty spoon. Keep going, there's more in there. Give it a good <kanji>shake</kanji>.
振.on: The heavy clam swings back on its chain and bangs him right on the <sound>shin</sound>.
振.kun: He hops around the deck and flops onto a <sound>fu</sound>ton, rubbing his sore leg.

総.meaning: In the <part>public</part> square, every person ties one <part>thread</part> from their own <part>heart</part> into a huge knot in the middle. No single thread is special; the knot belongs to the whole town. It's the <kanji>general</kanji> feeling of everyone.
総.on: When it rains, the town scrubs the whole knot with one giant bar of <sound>soa</sound>p that foams slowly for hours.
総.kun: Afterwards everyone shares one enormous plate of <sound>su</sound>shi, and every last piece of it gets eaten.

区.meaning: The city map is kept in a <part>drawer</part> at the town hall. One morning the mayor takes it out and, with a big pair of <part>scissors</part>, snips it into neat squares, one for each neighbourhood, each with its own mayor. Each piece is a <kanji>ward</kanji>.
区.on: Every ward gets its own <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock, and at noon they all chime at once across the city.

根.meaning: A gardening <part>robot</part> tries to pull up a <part>tree</part> to move it, but it won't budge. The robot digs and digs and finds long woody fingers gripping the earth, deeper and deeper, all the way under the house. That's only the first <kanji>root</kanji>.
根.on: A <sound>con</sound>dor swoops down, grabs the robot by its box head and helps it tug.
根.kun: In the end they wrap the roots in a fishing <sound>ne</sound>t and haul the whole tree out together.

材.meaning: A <part>genius</part> inventor needs planks, so she builds a machine that swallows a whole <part>tree</part> at one end and spits out perfect boards at the other, stacked and smelling of sap. Her yard is soon piled high with <kanji>lumber</kanji>.
材.on: With the very first boards she builds a giant <sound>xy</sound>lophone and plays it with two hammers.

考.meaning: An old man leans on his <part>cane</part> in front of a <part>stuck javelin</part> that has landed in his vegetable patch. Who threw it? Why? Should he pull it out or leave it? He strokes his beard and takes all afternoon to <kanji>consider</kanji>.
考.on: He thinks so long that the ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne in his other hand melts slowly down to his elbow.
考.kun: Still puzzling, he sniffs a pink <sound>carn</sound>ation and chews a clove of <sound>ga</sound>rlic, which always helps him think.

様.meaning: Under a <part>tree</part>, a very proper <part>sheep</part> in a top hat sips from a marble <part>fountain</part> while his butler bows low. Every letter that arrives for him is addressed with great politeness: Mr Fleece, <kanji>Esq.</kanji>
様.on: He is so grand that even his <sound>yo</sound>-yo is solid gold, and the butler spins it slowly down and up for him.
様.kun: For lunch the butler brings one <sound>sa</sound>rdine on a silver plate, and the sheep calls his <sound>ma</sound>ma to admire it.

存.meaning: A <part>child</part> lies in a tiny tent made of <part>one</part> plank, a <part>slash</part> of rope and a <part>pole</part>, staring up at the stars. What if there's a planet made of cake? What if dogs could talk? She lies there and wonders, and starts to <kanji>suppose</kanji>.
存.on: After an hour of supposing she's totally <sound>zon</sound>ked and falls asleep mid-thought.
存.kun: She supposes she'll live to a hundred on warm <sound>na</sound>an and <sound>ga</sound>rlic soup, with a crowd at every birthday shouting '<sound>Rah</sound>!': living on and on.

声.meaning: A tiny <part>gentleman</part> stands on top of a <part>flag</part> at the harbour and sings. He's no bigger than a thumb, yet ships turn round, dogs stop barking and seagulls land to listen. What a huge <kanji>voice</kanji>!
声.on: One high note is so loud it rattles a steel <sound>sa</sound>fe open on the dock below.
声.kun: A <sound>ko</sound>ala in the crow's nest is so startled that it drops its breakfast <sound>e</sound>gg.

給.meaning: At the end of each month, the tailor gets paid in gold <part>thread</part>, wound so neatly it will just <part>fit</part> into her purse. She can spend it at the market or weave it into a coat. Either way, it's her <kanji>salary</kanji>.
給.on: She spends her first one on a brand-new pool <sound>cue</sound> and wraps its handle in the gold thread.
給.kun: The rest goes on a <sound>ta</sound>co for herself and a bunch of flowers for her <sound>ma</sound>ma.

圧.meaning: A <part>cliff</part> leans out over a mound of <part>soil</part> and slowly sinks down onto it, squashing it flatter and flatter until it's hard as brick. Day after day it never lets up, not for a second. That's real <kanji>pressure</kanji>.
圧.on: Deep in the squashed soil, a worm gets dust up its nose: '<sound>Ah</sound>... <sound>tsu</sound>!'
圧.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps the worm, as the cliff pushes down on it once again.

種.meaning: A botanist finds a stalk of <part>grain</part> so <part>heavy</part> it bends right to the ground, each kernel the size of a plum. No book has ever drawn it. She names it after herself and dances around it: a brand-new <kanji>species</kanji>.
種.on: She bites a kernel, and it tastes as sweet as a <sound>su</sound>gar cube.
種.kun: She plants its seeds in an old <sound>ta</sound>co shell and covers them with a <sound>ne</sound>t to keep the birds off.

愛.meaning: A bear reaches down one <part>claw</part> and gently tucks a <part>blanket</part> around her cub, asleep on a <part>folding chair</part>. Then she draws a little <part>heart</part> in the dust with her fingertip. All that big, soft care is <kanji>love</kanji>.
愛.on: Overnight, <sound>i</sound>vy climbs up the chair legs and wraps both bears in green.
愛.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>!' squeals the cub at dawn, climbing to the <sound>to</sound>p of the chair to hug its dear mum.

可.meaning: A <part>street</part> sign has a tiny <part>mouth</part> tucked under its arm. Ask it anything, 'May I cross? May I skip? May I sing on the way?', and it always chirps the same cheerful answer: 'Yes, you <kanji>can</kanji>!'
可.on: Ask it whether a <sound>ca</sound>rp may cross the road, and even then it says yes.
可.kun: Ask it whether you should go to <sound>be</sound>d, and for once it says, 'You really ought to.'

想.meaning: Two inventors sit nose to nose, eyes locked in a <part>mutual</part> stare, until a spark jumps from <part>heart</part> to heart and a light bulb pops on over both their heads. They've had the very same brilliant <kanji>concept</kanji>.
想.on: Their idea: a bar of <sound>soa</sound>p that sings a long, slow song while you wash.
想.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' they both think next, picturing a <sound>mo</sound>p that cleans the bathroom by itself.

設.meaning: A <part>maiden</part> gives a rousing <part>speech</part> in an empty field, and as she talks, tents pop up, wells get dug and a bakery appears. By sunset every traveller has a bed, bread and water. She made <kanji>provision</kanji> for all.
設.on: A red <sound>set</sound>ter trots between the tents, handing out blankets from a basket in its mouth.
設.kun: Last of all she sets up a shed for the lawn<sound>mow</sound>er, to keep the campsite grass short.

置.meaning: A fisherman lowers his <part>net</part> onto the sand and lays each shell inside it in one <part>straight</part> line, checking with a ruler. Not a millimetre out of line. He fusses for hours over the <kanji>placement</kanji> of every one.
置.on: A <sound>chee</sound>tah sneaks up behind him and nudges one shell out of line, just to annoy him.
置.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' he groans, and puts it back exactly where it was.

演.meaning: In front of a tiny <part>shrine</part>, a frog in a velvet cape bows, then leaps through the <part>water drops</part> falling from the eaves while juggling three pebbles. A crowd of snails gasps and claps. What a <kanji>performance</kanji>!
演.on: For the finale he rides a toy steam <sound>en</sound>gine round the shrine, whistle blowing.

独.meaning: On a long <part>fishhook</part> dangles one lonely <part>insect</part>, the only bait in the whole lake. Shoals of fish swim past in a crowd, but nobody keeps it company. Just one bug, all by itself: <kanji>single</kanji>.
独.on: The fisherman has fallen asleep at the end of the empty <sound>dock</sound>, rod still in hand.
独.kun: The bug taps one <sound>hee</sound>l on the hook, then climbs to the <sound>to</sound>p of the line, alone.

申.meaning: A <part>pole</part> pierces the <part>sun</part> top to bottom, like a giant sundial pin. When its shadow touches the teacups painted on the town square, everyone stops for tea and cake, until the shadow reaches the dinner plates. That's the slot from <kanji>3-5PM</kanji>.
申.on: Every day at three, a waiter trips over the pole and bangs his <sound>shin</sound>, spilling the tea.
申.kun: Every day at five, a man on a <sound>mow</sound>er rides through the square and humbly says tea is over.
